title: Reducing the risk of geomorphological hazards

changes: Add a line to the card on aid and recovery after the event, since the brief includes aid after the event and the bank card does not mention it.
Make the evacuation wording match the brief's evacuation drills by mentioning practice drills alongside evacuation plans.
match.reason: The bank point covers the same idea at Year 8 depth, but it leaves out aid after the event and does not mention drills, so it needs small additions.

draft.title: Reducing the risk of hazards
card: A hazard cannot always be stopped, but the harm it does can be cut. Communities do this by preparing before the event, acting during it and helping people afterwards.
detect a hazard and alert people in time to move. A tsunami warning system, for example, can send out alerts after an undersea earthquake.
Earthquake-resistant buildings are designed to flex and stay standing. Land-use planning keeps homes and schools away from high-risk places, such as steep slopes and coasts.
Evacuation drills teach people where to go and what to do. Aid after the event, such as food, shelter and medical help, helps a community recover.
draft.remember: Communities cut the harm from hazards by preparing, warning, planning and helping afterwards.

a.q: A coastal town holds regular practice runs so that residents know the route to high ground. Which method of reducing risk is this?
a.why: Practice runs that teach people where to go and what to do are evacuation drills. Land-use planning is tempting, but it controls where buildings are placed rather than teaching people how to respond.
a.clue: The residents are practising what to do.

b.q: Council in a hilly town bans new homes on steep slopes that have slid before. How does this reduce the harm from landslides?
opts: It keeps people and buildings out of high-risk places
It alerts people in time to leave their homes
It helps the community recover after a landslide
It makes buildings flex and stay standing in a landslide
b.why: Banning homes on slopes that have slid before is land-use planning. It keeps people and buildings away from the hazard in the first place. A warning system alerts people, and aid helps recovery, but neither is what a ban on building does.
b.clue: The ban decides where buildings can go.

b.best: It keeps people and buildings out of high-risk places
